blocks.md: This lesson covers the book's section on **Exercises**. Read the excerpt, then test yourself below.

All quantities below are hypothetical problem givens, chosen to be round, and describe no particular model, provider, or deployment. Unless a problem says otherwise, assume step errors are independent, each attempt costs the same in expectation, and "accepted" means accepted under a fixed task contract.

blocks.prompt: Think first: In two or three sentences, explain why Cost per accepted task matters for the system this section describes.
blocks.md: Compare your answer with the book's claim: Under retry-until-accept, C_eff = E[C_attempt]/p_acc, so acceptance divides the whole attempt cost and any mechanism pays for its overhead only if it lowers this ratio.

questions.q: The section **Exercises** develops one of the chapter's claims. Which one?
options: Constraints never rest on the model: bounds close mechanically below it and acceptance rests on external evidence above it, and greater exposure demands stronger closure.
The characteristic agent failure is well-formed, credible, and wrong, so fail-stop monitors record success and agreement among samples from one model sets no bound on wrong answers.
Every side effect passes an explicit runtime-checked grant and evidence comes only from tools and deterministic checks, never from model text.
Under retry-until-accept, C_eff = E[C_attempt]/p_acc, so acceptance divides the whole attempt cost and any mechanism pays for its overhead only if it lowers this ratio.
